newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Q3 growth rate seen steady at 1-2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Q3 growth rate seen steady at 1-2 pct.

text.p: Estonian economic forecasters believe growth in the third quarter of 1996 was not much changed from the one to two percent year-on-year rise of the first half, the Estonian Institute for Market Research said on Tuesday.

The organisation also predicted in its latest bulletin that there would be annual growth of three to five percent over the next three to five years for the Baltic state, compared with a gross domestic product (GDP) rise of three percent in 1995.
"There is no clear proof that the first-half growth of one to two percent has improved during July, August and September," the institute, which gathers the forecasts of economists, said.
It said that growth is being hindered by the low competitiveness of goods and services on the international market, a shortage of capital, a small domestic market and a lack of skilled workers.
The sectors having the most problems with development are the energy and industry areas while banking and communicatins are developing well, the report added.

The institute also forecast rising exports and imports in the next six months but most of its experts expected either an unchanged or worsening trade deficit. Estonia's trade deficit has hovered around one billion kroon for most of the year.
